ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a large equilateral triangle with a horizontal base, and there is also a regular pentagon overlapping the interior and upper area of the triangle. The base of the regular pentagon is on the same horizontal line as the base of the triangle. The marked angle x is located at the intersection of the left slanted side of the triangle and the lower-left side of the regular pentagon, and what is marked in the figure is the larger obtuse angle. Reasoning: Each interior angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, so its left slanted side forms 60° with the direction of the horizontal base. Each interior angle of a regular pentagon is 108°, therefore the direction turning from the base toward the right to the direction of the lower-left side of the regular pentagon forms 108°. The acute angle between the two intersecting straight lines is 108° - 60° = 48°. The marked x in the figure is the supplementary angle of this acute angle, so x = 180° - 48° = 132°.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram shows an equilateral triangle and a regular pentagon. What is the value of $x$?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as an equilateral triangle with a horizontal bottom side, and a regular pentagon whose bottom side lies on the same horizontal line. Identify the marked angle x at the crossing of the triangle’s left side and the pentagon’s lower-left side. From the text, use that the triangle is equilateral, so its left side makes 60° with the horizontal base. Also use that a regular pentagon has interior angle 108°, so the pentagon’s lower-left side makes 108° with the base direction to the right. The acute angle between the two crossing lines is 108° − 60° = 48°. The marked angle is the obtuse supplementary angle at the intersection, so x = 180° − 48° = 132°.

method.method_draft: Focus on the small triangle on the lower-left of the diagram bounded by the outer triangle’s left side, the pentagon’s lower-left side, and the bottom base segment between their two bottom endpoints. From the image, the marked x is outside/supplementary to the top angle of this small triangle. The angle at the left base endpoint is 60° because the large triangle is equilateral. At the pentagon’s lower-left base vertex, the angle inside the small triangle is the exterior angle of the regular pentagon at that vertex, equal to 180° − 108° = 72°. Therefore the small triangle’s top angle is 180° − 60° − 72° = 48°. Since x is supplementary to that top angle, x = 180° − 48° = 132°.
